bullets.title: Massive NVDA rally after Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO with White House backing
bullets.body: NVIDIA's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO, and Board Director after receiving input from senior U.S. government officials confirming no national security risk. NVDA shares surged 31.5% Monday, the largest Nasdaq opening gap since 2000, adding ~$950B in market cap and triggering a broad AI ecosystem rally (SMH +15%, AI Neoclouds +16-17%). Key overhangs remain: ongoing board/SEC investigations, bipartisan Congressional vows to impose tighter chip export controls (MATCH Act, Chip Security Act), Jensen's scheduled Senate Banking Committee testimony Dec 3, and California AG criminal probe continuing.

bullets.title: S&P 500 finished week +5.6%, Nasdaq +6.7% — but rally seen as tactical, not fundamental
bullets.body: The S&P 500 gained ~5.6% and Nasdaq ~6.7% for the week, with Tech sector +7.3%, snapping a seven-session losing streak. Multiple strategists (22V, JPM, GS) characterized the bounce as positioning-driven short-covering rather than a durable inflection: hedge fund net exposure was near multi-year lows (~39-42%), CTA positioning was net short, and retail flows were the weakest since Jan 2025. Decisive close above SPX 7,350–7,400 would be needed to confirm a durable low; Friday's holiday-shortened session closed at ~7,271.

bullets.title: Fed hawkishness is the dominant macro constraint — no pivot in sight
bullets.body: Core PCE came in at 0.293% MoM (+3.26% YoY) in October, with nominal GDP running ~6.3% — far too strong for the Fed's 2% target. Q3 GDP was revised sharply upward to 4.3% from 3.4%, driven by AI-related capex and consumer spending. Multiple strategists (22V, JPM, MS) emphasized the Fed has shifted from tolerating ~2.5% core PCE to explicitly targeting 2%, moving the 'Fed put' much further away. Markets are pricing three consecutive 25bp hikes through Q1 2027. Financial conditions have tightened ~35bp since the equity drawdown began.

bullets.title: AI capex debate intensifies: token price collapse, GPU offloads, neocloud credit stress
bullets.body: SpaceX cut spot GPU rental rates 20-35% (B300 to $10-12/hr from $15.50); AI token pricing fell 21% over the past month; and CoreWeave bonds hit record lows with CDS implying 70%+ 5-year default probability. AI token demand elasticity collapsed from 5.4 (Q1) to 1.2 (Q4), and Jevons Paradox appears broken for AI — inference costs are falling but usage isn't spiking correspondingly. Goldman estimates $705B in AI debt YTD with more supply expected in 2027. Lenders stalled billions in data center financing tied to ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent after new BIS chip export rules.

bullets.title: BIS export controls shut down SE Asia GPU shipments; NVDA halts server deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia
bullets.body: The November 16 BIS interim final rule closed the China remote-access loophole for advanced NVIDIA chips and added destination-based licensing for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. NVIDIA asked server partners to halt shipments in those markets. Malaysia alone had a 10GW data center plan with >50% serving Chinese hyperscalers. TSMC and Samsung also halted <16nm shipments to Chinese-designed chips. The 90-day compliance window for existing Chinese customer relationships is creating urgency across the data center financing ecosystem, with banks pulling exposure.

bullets.title: DRAM/NAND cycle outlook darkens: TrendForce cuts 2027 forecasts, 2028 broad downturn flagged
bullets.body: TrendForce revised 1Q27 DRAM contract price growth to +3-8% QoQ from +5-10%, with 2H27 expected flat and LPDDR4X/consumer DRAM falling 5-10% in 4Q27. The 2028 base case anticipates broad conventional DRAM price declines from 1Q28, with the bear case seeing declines exceeding 15% QoQ. NAND bit supply is projected to grow 29% in 2027 vs. 19% demand growth, with 4Q27 ASPs declining 20-25% YoY. Chinese CSPs began cutting 2027 server DRAM bit demand outside LTAs in 4Q26, with North American CSPs absorbing the slack. HBM remains the bright spot at 80% YoY bit demand growth.

bullets.title: Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners coming; effective US tariff rate to rise to 9-10%
bullets.body: The US is preparing to institute Section 301 tariffs on 14 major trading partners including China (up to 20% on most goods), EU, Japan, Vietnam (up to 35%), India (25%), and Singapore (20%). JPMorgan expects the effective US tariff rate to rise from 6.5% in September to 9-9.5%, potentially back toward 10%. Semiconductors, servers, smartphones, PCs, storage, and chips are on Section 301 exemption lists, largely protecting the AI supply chain. However, semiconductor testing suppliers face tariff exposure.

bullets.title: Dell blowout Q3 — $132B AI backlog, raises FY27 to $202B revenue, $29.68 EPS
bullets.body: Dell reported Q3 revenue of $54.94B (+103% YoY) vs. $49.32B consensus and EPS of $9.45 vs. $6.60 consensus. AI-optimized server revenue reached $22B with $60.2B in new orders; the backlog expanded to a record $132.3B (+40% QoQ). Management raised FY27 guidance to $202B revenue (+78% YoY) and $29.68 EPS (+188% YoY), with AI server revenue guided to $78B. The board authorized an additional $25B in buybacks. Supply-demand gap is expected to widen into FY28 with enterprise NAND/DRAM pricing staying elevated.

bullets.title: CrowdStrike acquires Zscaler for $43.9B all-stock; cybersecurity consolidation accelerates
bullets.body: CrowdStrike announced an all-stock acquisition of Zscaler valued at ~$43.9B (1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share), expected to close H2 FY2028. CRWD simultaneously reported a record Q3 with NNARR of $419M (+58% YoY) and ARR of $6.26B (+27% YoY) — the fifth consecutive quarter of acceleration. The combined entity targets ~$1B annualized revenue synergies by 30 months post-close. ZS's network enforcement capabilities fill a gap in Falcon's AI-agent security stack. The deal is seen as the catalyst for accelerated M&A across cybersecurity (OKTA, NTSK, SAIL flagged as takeout candidates).

bullets.title: China equity stabilization measures seen as insufficient without more aggressive fiscal stimulus
bullets.body: The CSI 300 rallied 4.2% and the STAR 50 tech index surged 15% on State Council signals of stepped-up capital market support, but the CSI 300 remains down 19.7% from its June peak. 22V Research is skeptical that incremental 'national team' buying can sustain a rally without more aggressive fiscal policy, noting STAR 50 trades at trailing P/E of 100x. Key December meetings (Politburo, Central Economic Work Conference Dec 8-16) are unlikely to signal a major policy shift. JPM China GDP growth forecast for 2027 is 4.5%, with housing entering its sixth consecutive year of downturn.

bullets.title: Global capex nowcast strong at 9.4% annualized; AI capex doubling to $1.4T in 2027 but growth decelerating
bullets.body: JPMorgan's capex nowcaster shows 4Q26 tracking at 9.4% SAAR, with developed markets at 10.2% and EM ex-China at 17.3%. Separately, JPM's AI capex model projects $1.4T in 2027 AI capex (nearly doubling from 2026) across 23 GW under construction and 97 GW committed. However, growth rates are expected to decelerate materially in 2028+, and the equity financing share is rising as debt markets near capacity ($476B in AI capex financing in 2026 alone). Power remains the critical bottleneck for data center construction.

bullets.title: October PCE data: core 3.26% YoY, real consumer spending flat — Q4 tracking 1.7% annualized
bullets.body: October core PCE rose 0.293% MoM (+3.26% YoY), in line with consensus, but upward revisions to August/September were noted. Real PCE was essentially flat in October, missing expectations, with Q4 real PCE now tracking ~1.7% annualized vs. a prior 2.5% estimate. Nominal disposable income beat at +0.73% MoM, with the savings rate rising to 4.1% from 3.6%. The October goods trade deficit widened to $149.5B on a 65% YoY surge in capital goods imports, which could subtract from 4Q GDP if sustained.

bullets.title: Q3 profit margins at all-time highs; labor share collapse in tech is the primary driver
bullets.body: Q3 US corporate profits rose 4.4% QoQ (21% YoY before-tax) with domestic non-financial pretax profits up 5.2% QoQ and 23% YoY. National profit margins hit record highs at 17.4%, up 1.8pp YoY, driven primarily by labor share compression in tech. Outside tech, margins also advanced in Q2 and Q3, with energy a past contributor. Analysts warn that profit growth slowdown seems inevitable if nominal value added growth slows, and AI efficiency gains that lower token prices could undermine the operating leverage that has driven tech margins.

bullets.title: EM outflows accelerating; Taiwan saw $65B+ net outflows over seven weeks; EM passive holds
bullets.body: EM equity fund inflows slowed to $767M last week from $2.4B prior, marking the eighth consecutive week of positive passive flows even as MSCI EM fell 16.5% — the worst performance over any inflows streak in history. Active funds posted $1.6B in outflows. Taiwan saw $6.8B in outflows (seventh consecutive week, $65B+ total), driven by AI/semiconductor liquidation. India accelerated to +$3.3B inflows. EM ex-China flows stayed positive for a 13th consecutive week. Korean and Taiwanese chip export data remains robust YoY, suggesting equity weakness is positioning-driven, not fundamental.

bullets.title: ECB and BoE both expected to hike more; IG Metall deal provides wage inflation relief for 2028
bullets.body: The ECB's October minutes showed a 'large number' of Governing Council members were prepared to hike despite holding, and JPM expects two more hikes before a 2028 potential pivot. The IG Metall 25-month pay deal (2.0-2.3% annual raises, 2.4-2.8% in 2027, 1.7-2.2% in 2028) is well below current inflation and significantly reduces upside wage risk for 2028. The BoE is expected to hike twice more (February and April 2027) to reach 4.5%, with CPI set to peak above 4% in H1 2027 due to energy shock. France's economy contracted 1.0% QoQ in Q3 and is in technical recession.

bullets.title: JPM and MS 2027 S&P 500 targets: 8,200 (JPM) and 8,700 (MS) on 14-17% EPS growth
bullets.body: JPMorgan sets a 2027 S&P 500 target of 8,200 based on $430 EPS (+17% YoY) and re-rating to 19x, with AI accounting for ~67% of 2027 earnings growth. Morgan Stanley targets 8,700 based on 14% EPS growth, with the Fed funds range at 4.25-4.50% and the 10-year at 5%. Both houses see AI as the structural growth engine but acknowledge the correction has significantly derisked the entry point: SPX forward P/E has compressed from ~23x to ~16.5x. Key downside risks: policy error from Fed overtightening, data center regulatory friction, and rising cost of capital for neocloud financing.

bullets.title: Consumer confidence jumps to highest since Jan 2025; retail earnings beat broadly
bullets.body: November Consumer Confidence jumped 11.4 points to 103.3, the highest since January 2025, driven by improved labor market perceptions and lower gas prices (-4.1% WoW). Weekly Redbook retail sales accelerated to +11.3% YoY. Retailers beat across the board: BBY reported Q3 comps +6.1%, DLTR traffic accelerated to +3.8%, ANF posted comps +6%, KSS returned to positive comps for the first time in years, and DKS raised FY26 guidance. High-income consumer remains resilient; low-income remains pressured. Retail credit card data for November shows modest deceleration to +1.6% WoW vs. +2.1% 6-week average.

bullets.title: BoJ on track for more hikes; Japan core CPI rose to 2.9% — constructive for yen
bullets.body: Tokyo core CPI rose to 2.9% YoY, a 16-month high, bolstering the case for a BoJ December rate hike. JPMorgan forecasts BoJ rates reaching 2% through mid-2027 and 2.25% by year-end, with negative real rates limiting near-term economic drag. Japan's $10T fiscal expansion and AI-related capex demand are adding to inflationary pressure. JPM FX strategy is tactically bullish yen but medium-term cautious; USD/JPY support at 152-154. Korea and Taiwan fiscal impulses exceed 2% of GDP; BoK delivered a hawkish 25bp hike with further expected.

bullets.title: AI adoption early but accelerating; compute demand estimated at 5x available supply
bullets.body: Goldman's European AI symposium estimated AI workplace usage at 10-20%, with only 2.2% of US households holding paid AI subscriptions, while compute demand is ~5x available supply. Agentic AI workloads surged from <10% of token consumption in February to ~80% in October. JPM APAC conference noted 25x YoY token consumption growth and supply chains gearing up at full capacity for a 2-3 year compute ramp. Morgan Stanley's 'Europe AI 50' framework identifies the continent's strength in application-layer software with regulated domain expertise, not compute infrastructure.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning near multi-year lows; AI/semis short interest at record highs — setup for reversal
bullets.body: Goldman noted short exposure in AI stocks at multi-year highs, with momentum exposure swung to net short from +70% in June. HF net leverage fell to 39-42% (bottom decile since 2010). CTA net positioning in tech was near the most bearish since April 2025. US Semis saw ~3 standard deviation net selling over 20 trading days. JPM's positioning strategist noted that if stabilization occurs, Beta, Cyclicals, and Semis could significantly outperform Quality as the squeeze unwinds — but a durable bottom requires a shift from short-covering to genuine long demand.
